title: Seeded owned apps
summary: The Nivo backend idempotently seeds an Expert Academy app and an MMO app for the fixed demo account so the existing generic owned-instance query can expose both without provisioning MMO infrastructure or inventing MMO product features.

includes: Idempotent demo-owned instance seed for tester@nivo.local
One seeded ai_academy instance labelled Học viện Chuyên gia
One seeded mmo instance labelled MMO
Generic myInstances projection for both seeded rows
excludes: MMO provisioning, chart installation, DNS publication or deployment
MMO catalogue purchase or pricing tiers
MMO-specific product detail tables, operations or control-center behavior
Production users other than the fixed demo account

actors.label: Fixed Nivo demo account owner
capabilities: See the seeded Expert Academy and MMO instances through the existing owned-app query

flows.title: Seed demo-owned apps
flows.trigger: The Nivo backend completes application bootstrap

steps.action: The backend resolves the fixed demo account
steps.result: Seeding skips safely when the account does not exist

steps.action: The backend upserts the two declared owned instances
steps.result: Exactly one Expert Academy row and one MMO row are owned by the demo account

steps.action: The authenticated demo owner requests myInstances
steps.result: Both seeded app identities are returned through the generic instance projection

outcomes: The frontend can render Học viện Chuyên gia and MMO as two current owned apps without provisioning MMO infrastructure

rules.statement: The demo seed is idempotent and scoped only to tester@nivo.local; a missing demo account is a safe skip.
The MMO seed binds the existing mmo provisionable-app registry identity but remains non-provisionable and has no product-detail row.
Owned apps are exposed through the generic instance spine; adding MMO does not add an MMO branch to myInstances.

operations.name: seedDemoOwnedApps
outputs: idempotently persisted academy and MMO instances

operations.name: myInstances
outputs: owned app key, instance identity, name, plan, resources and status

surfaces.title: Owned apps feed
surfaces.purpose: Supply the authenticated owner's current app instances to the console Apps flow.

regions.title: Current apps
regions.summary: The generic owned-instance projection contains the two declared demo-owned app identities.

acceptance.statement: Repeated backend boot does not duplicate either seeded owned app for tester@nivo.local.
myInstances returns one ai_academy row labelled Học viện Chuyên gia and one mmo row labelled MMO for the demo owner.
The MMO seed creates no provisioning request, deployment, chart install, catalogue order or MMO-specific detail row.

unknowns.question: Which product-specific regions and operations will an MMO control center eventually own?
unknowns.impact: The backend may expose the seeded MMO instance through myInstances, but design and implementation must not invent MMO-specific management behavior.

unknowns.question: Which deterministic local hostname, resource allocation, plan and version snapshot should the seed use for each instance?
unknowns.impact: Backend planning must choose values compatible with the existing InstanceEntity without treating them as product pricing or provisioning claims.

evidence.claim: The existing primary-database demo seeder resolves tester@nivo.local, skips safely when absent and idempotently updates or inserts demo-owned rows.
The provisionable-app registry already defines ai_academy and a deliberately non-provisionable mmo identity with no chart, host, pipeline or product-specific detail contract.
myInstances reads instances as the generic spine, joins the app registry and maps any app key, name, plan, resources and status without an app-specific branch.
The query test proves an MMO instance with no product enum or detail table is returned as appKey mmo through the generic owned-instance response.
The owner requested that Nivo backend assume an MMO app exists and provide seed data for two current apps, Học viện Chuyên gia and MMO, without provisioning.
